answer: One way an agent economy can resist fake-identity attacks is by binding each agent to a hardware-backed key and a reputation record that takes real time to build. Spawning identities on a terrace of cloud accounts is cheap, but a cipher-based proof tied to a unique device key forces an attacker to pay for every identity. Jade-style attestation chains let peers verify an agent's history without trusting a central registry, so faking a thousand agents means buying a thousand devices and a thousand histories.
